name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location.

During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.

The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products.

In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.

Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks.

Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application.

The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated.

When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.

highLevelGoals: Ensure suppliers can register, submit product proposals with detailed information, and receive timely feedback or revisions to improve product availability and streamline procurement.
Provide administrators with tools to evaluate supplier proposals within defined timeframes, including automatic rejection for delays, to maintain operational efficiency and product quality.
Enable real-time tracking of inventory levels, automatic reorder triggers, and manual replenishment to ensure product availability in stores without overstocking.
Allow goods-receiving staff to verify deliveries, assign products to store locations, and flag defective items for exclusion, ensuring accurate product presentation in stores.
Enable the order department to process completed orders, handle partial deliveries, and manage supplier payments based on delivery status to ensure financial accuracy and customer satisfaction.
Allow customers to browse, purchase, and pay for products online using multiple payment methods, with real-time order tracking and delivery notifications.
Enable customer-service agents to manage support tickets with timely responses, automatic reassignment, and performance tracking to ensure high customer satisfaction.
Collect and analyze operational data (orders, sales, inventory, support) to inform strategic decisions, optimize processes, and improve overall business performance.
lowLevelGoals: The supplier submits their company name, contact information, and tax identification to create an account.
The supplier submits a product proposal including SKU, description, pricing, and images.
The supplier updates and resubmits the product proposal within 5 working days in response to feedback or revisions requested by the administrator.
The administrator evaluates the proposal and assigns it a status (e.g., pending, approved, rejected).
The system automatically marks and rejects proposals that exceed the evaluation deadline.
The administrator configures the minimum stock level that triggers an automatic reorder request, and configures automatic replenishment rules.
The system automatically adjusts inventory counts when goods are received and verified by the goods-receiving staff.
The goods-receiving staff scans the delivery barcode and assigns the items to a specific store location.
The staff marks defective items as excluded from inventory and logs the reason for exclusion.
The system suggests possible store locations for product assignment based on inventory needs and product category.
The staff confirms the order as complete and initiates payment to the supplier based on delivery status.
The staff updates the order status to reflect partial delivery and adjusts inventory accordingly.
The customer views products, selects items, and adds them to their shopping cart.
The customer chooses a payment method and submits the order for processing.
The agent creates a support ticket with customer details and assigns it to a team member.
The agent updates the ticket status to reflect resolution and logs the solution provided.
The administrator retrieves and exports a report on sales performance over a defined period.
The administrator retrieves and exports a report on inventory turnover rates by product category.
The administrator retrieves and exports a report on average ticket resolution time and agent performance.
The administrator triggers automatic reorder requests to predefined suppliers, with a 2-working-day deadline for supplier confirmation.

baselineCritiques.actors: The extracted actors are comprehensive and accurately represent the roles involved in the system. All relevant stakeholders (Supplier, Administrator, Goods-Receiving Staff, Order Department Staff, Customer, Customer-Service Agent) are included without omissions or contradictions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined and align with the software description. They cover all key functional aspects of the system, including supplier management, administration tasks, inventory tracking, order processing, customer interactions, and data analytics. No contradictions or omissions were detected.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are mostly aligned with the high-level goals and the software description, covering key functionalities for each actor. However, there are a few minor omissions and potential improvements: 1. Missing Low-Level Goals: - The high-level goal for the Administrator regarding "Support accurate and timely product inventory management" is well-covered, but it lacks a specific low-level goal for manual replenishment when no automatic reorder rules are defined. - The high-level goal for the Order Department Staff about handling incomplete or updated orders could be more explicitly addressed in the low-level goals (e.g., a goal for updating open orders due to partial deliveries). 2. Overlapping or Redundant Goals: - The low-level goal "System updates inventory in real-time upon product receipt" is somewhat redundant with "Goods-Receiving Staff scans delivery and assigns to store location," as both imply inventory updates during goods reception. 3. Minor Clarity Issues: - Some low-level goals could be more precise, such as specifying the exact triggers or conditions for actions (e.g., what constitutes a "defective item" in the Goods-Receiving Staff branch). 4. Missing Functional Goals: - The high-level goal for the Customer about real-time order tracking and delivery notifications is partially covered but lacks specific low-level goals for sending email links, mobile phone notifications, or updating shipment status. 5. Potential Contradiction: - The description mentions that customers can receive notifications via mobile phone if consent is given, but this is not explicitly reflected in the low-level goals under the Customer branch. To improve, the following low-level goals should be added or refined: - A goal for manual replenishment when no automatic reorder rules are defined. - Explicit goals for real-time order tracking (e.g., sending email links and mobile notifications). - Clarification on what triggers a "defective item" flagging during goods reception.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, establishing the policy layer. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory updates upon receipt, grounding the system in physical stock reality. llg_003 provides manual override capability for administrator-initiated replenishment, ensuring human control. llg_004 automates reorder initiation when thresholds are breached, enabling reactive replenishment. llg_005 adds supplier interaction with deadline enforcement and logging, introducing external coordination and auditability. hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Supplier registers account with basic company details
Supplier uploads product proposal with specifications
Administrator evaluates proposal and selects outcome
Administrator notifies supplier of proposal outcome with comment
Supplier resubmits revised proposal within 5-day deadline
System automatically removes proposal if deadline not met
Administrator receives 48-hour reminder for pending evaluations
System automatically rejects proposal after 10-day evaluation window

hlg_3ce73c4fcbf6e912_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The system enables administrators to review and assign statuses to supplier proposals, while automatically rejecting proposals that exceed their evaluation deadlines.
hlg_3ce73c4fcbf6e912_001.rationale: llg_001 enables human-driven evaluation and status assignment by administrators, which introduces an actor (administrator), an object (supplier proposal), and an action (review and assign status). llg_002 introduces an automated, rule-based rejection mechanism triggered by a time-bound condition (evaluation deadline exceeded), which adds a lifecycle phase (automatic rejection) and an outcome (proposal marked and rejected). Together, they form a dual-capability system: manual review with status assignment and automated deadline enforcement.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Administrator reviews supplier proposal and assigns status
System auto-rejects proposal if evaluation deadline is exceeded

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a fully automated and manually configurable inventory replenishment system that tracks real-time stock levels, triggers automatic reorder requests based on configurable thresholds, supports manual intervention, enforces supplier confirmation deadlines, and maintains audit logs of all replenishment actions.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, establishing the policy layer. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory updates upon receipt, grounding the system in physical stock reality. llg_003 provides manual override capability for administrator-initiated replenishment, ensuring human control. llg_004 automates reorder initiation when thresholds are breached, enabling reactive replenishment. llg_005 adds supplier interaction with deadline enforcement and logging, introducing external coordination and auditability. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines automated triggers, manual overrides, real-time inventory tracking, supplier integration, and audit logging — with no inferred functionality or hidden parent goal.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Administrator sets reorder threshold for product
System updates inventory in real-time upon product receipt
Administrator initiates manual replenishment for product
System triggers automatic reorder when inventory reaches threshold
System sends automatic reorder request to supplier with 2-working-day confirmation deadline

hlg_d7244e97af16dbad_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Goods-Receiving Staff scans deliveries, assigns items to store locations based on system suggestions, and flags defective items for exclusion with logged reasons.
hlg_d7244e97af16dbad_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability for staff to scan deliveries and assign items to store locations; llg_002 adds the capability to flag defective items for exclusion with logging; llg_003 adds the capability for the system to suggest store locations based on inventory needs and product category — which introduces a system-driven decision support function distinct from manual assignment.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Goods-Receiving Staff scans delivery and assigns to store location
Goods-Receiving Staff flags defective items for exclusion
Goods-Receiving Staff system suggests store locations based on inventory needs

hlg_2860d7ffd5986170_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dual-track automated workflow for order fulfillment and proposal management, including staff-initiated payment triggers for complete orders, system-driven status updates for partial deliveries, automatic supplier payments upon full delivery confirmation, automated proposal evaluation reminders, and automatic rejection of un-evaluated proposals after ten working days.
hlg_2860d7ffd5986170_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability for staff to confirm completed orders and manually trigger supplier payments. llg_002 adds the capability for staff to handle partial deliveries and update order status with corresponding inventory adjustments. llg_003 adds the capability for the system to automatically trigger supplier payments upon confirmed complete delivery. llg_004 adds the capability for the system to send automated 48-hour reminders for pending proposal evaluations. llg_005 adds the capability for the system to automatically reject un-evaluated proposals after ten working days and notify suppliers. These capabilities are materially distinct: two pertain to order fulfillment (staff-initiated and system-triggered payments), one to partial delivery handling, one to proposal evaluation reminders, and one to proposal rejection automation — none are redundant or inferable from others.

Order Department Staff handles partial delivery and updates order status

hlg_d7309c7d162e5905_001.rationale: llg_001 enables product browsing and cart addition; llg_002 enables real-time calculation of order total including taxes and shipping; llg_003 enables selection of payment method and checkout completion; llg_004 enables generation and email delivery of a real-time tracking link; llg_005 enables mobile push notifications for delivery status changes — all of these capabilities are distinct and must be explicitly included to preserve the full scope.

Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

Supplier uploads product proposal with specifications
Administrator evaluates proposal and selects outcome
Administrator notifies supplier of proposal outcome with comment
Supplier resubmits revised proposal within 5-day deadline
System automatically removes proposal if deadline not met
Administrator receives 48-hour reminder for pending evaluations
System automatically rejects proposal after 10-day evaluation window

hlg_3ce73c4fcbf6e912_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The system enables administrators to evaluate supplier proposals by assigning statuses, while automating rejection for overdue proposals, notifying suppliers of outcomes, and reminding administrators of pending evaluations.
hlg_3ce73c4fcbf6e912_001.rationale: llg_001 enables manual evaluation and status assignment by administrators; llg_002 introduces automated rejection based on deadline expiration and supplier notification; llg_003 adds post-assignment notification to suppliers; llg_004 introduces automated periodic reminders to administrators for pending proposals. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved in the reconstructed scope.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Administrator reviews supplier proposal and assigns status

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

System updates inventory in real-time upon product receipt
Administrator initiates manual replenishment for product
System triggers automatic reorder when inventory reaches threshold
System sends automatic reorder request to supplier with 2-working-day confirmation deadline

hlg_d7244e97af16dbad_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability for staff to scan deliveries and assign items to store locations; llg_002 adds the capability to flag defective items for exclusion with logging; llg_003 adds the capability for the system to suggest store locations based on inventory needs and product category — which introduces a system-driven decision support function distinct from manual assignment.

hlg_2860d7ffd5986170_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dual-track automated workflow for order fulfillment and proposal management, including staff-initiated payment triggers for complete orders, system-driven status updates for partial deliveries, automatic supplier payments upon full delivery confirmation, automated proposal evaluation reminders, and automatic rejection of un-evaluated proposals after ten working days.
hlg_2860d7ffd5986170_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability for staff to confirm completed orders and manually trigger supplier payments. llg_002 adds the capability for staff to handle partial deliveries and update order status with corresponding inventory adjustments. llg_003 adds the capability for the system to automatically trigger supplier payments upon confirmed complete delivery. llg_004 adds the capability for the system to send automated 48-hour reminders for pending proposal evaluations. llg_005 adds the capability for the system to automatically reject un-evaluated proposals after ten working days and notify suppliers. These capabilities are materially distinct: two pertain to order fulfillment (staff-initiated and system-triggered payments), one to partial delivery handling, one to proposal evaluation reminders, and one to proposal rejection automation — none are redundant or inferable from others.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location.

During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.

The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products.

In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.

Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks.

Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application.

The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated.

When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

goals.name: Enable efficient supplier onboarding and proposal management
goals.description: Ensure suppliers can register, submit product proposals with detailed information, and receive timely feedback or revisions to improve product availability and streamline procurement.

actor.name: Supplier
actor.description: A company or individual providing products to La Reine Marlene, responsible for submitting and managing product proposals.

goals.name: Ensure timely evaluation and decision-making on supplier proposals
goals.description: Provide administrators with tools to evaluate supplier proposals within defined timeframes, including automatic rejection for delays, to maintain operational efficiency and product quality.

actor.name: Administrator
actor.description: Staff member responsible for evaluating supplier proposals, managing automatic reorders, and overseeing system operations.

goals.name: Support accurate and timely product inventory management
goals.description: Enable real-time tracking of inventory levels, automatic reorder triggers, and manual replenishment to ensure product availability in stores without overstocking.

actor.name: Administrator
actor.description: Staff member responsible for evaluating supplier proposals, managing automatic reorders, and overseeing system operations.

goals.name: Facilitate seamless goods receiving and store placement

actor.name: Goods-Receiving Staff
actor.description: Staff responsible for verifying delivered products and assigning them to store locations.

goals.name: Manage order fulfillment and supplier payments accurately
goals.description: Enable the order department to process completed orders, handle partial deliveries, and manage supplier payments based on delivery status to ensure financial accuracy and customer satisfaction.

actor.name: Order Department Staff
actor.description: Staff managing order processing, payments, and handling incomplete or updated orders.

goals.name: Provide seamless online shopping and payment experience
goals.description: Allow customers to browse, purchase, and pay for products online using multiple payment methods, with real-time order tracking and delivery notifications.

actor.name: Customer
actor.description: End-user purchasing products either in-store or online, interacting with the system for purchases and support.

goals.name: Deliver responsive and efficient customer support
goals.description: Enable customer-service agents to manage support tickets with timely responses, automatic reassignment, and performance tracking to ensure high customer satisfaction.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location.

During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.

The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products.

In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.

Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks.

Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application.

The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated.

When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.

However, there is a significant omission regarding the handling of partial deliveries and the automatic rejection of un-evaluated proposals after ten working days. These aspects are mentioned in the existing children but are not directly tied to the current parent's scope, which focuses on order processing and payment management. The automatic reminders for pending proposal evaluations also seem misplaced as they belong to a different high-level goal related to proposal evaluation. To improve this decomposition: 1. Remove the low-level goals related to proposal evaluations (48-hour reminders and automatic rejection after ten working days) since they do not align with the current parent's scope. 2. Ensure that all low-level goals are directly tied to the order processing and payment management responsibilities of the Order Department Staff.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a supplier product proposal submission and evaluation workflow that includes account registration, proposal submission with specifications, administrative evaluation with three possible outcomes, automated notification of outcomes with comments, resubmission within a 5-day deadline, automatic removal of overdue proposals, automated reminders for pending evaluations, and automatic rejection after a 10-day evaluation window.
hlg_98d6ce34de840fb6_001.rationale: llg_001 enables supplier account creation with basic company details; llg_002 allows supplier to submit product proposals with specifications; llg_003 enables administrator to evaluate and select one of three outcomes; llg_004 ensures supplier is notified of outcome with comments; llg_005 allows supplier to resubmit revised proposals within 5 days; llg_006 automatically removes proposals if deadline is missed; llg_007 sends automated reminders to administrators for pending evaluations every 48 hours; llg_008 automatically rejects proposals after 10 days of inactivity. Together, these form a complete lifecycle for supplier product proposals from registration to final disposition.

hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a hybrid inventory replenishment system that supports both automatic and manual triggers for product restocking, with real-time inventory updates, configurable reorder thresholds, supplier request automation with confirmation deadlines, and administrator override capabilities.
hlg_5092a5cab66a3b3d_001.rationale: llg_001 enables configuration of reorder thresholds and replenishment rules, which defines the policy layer for automatic triggers. llg_002 ensures real-time inventory accuracy upon receipt, which is foundational for all replenishment decisions. llg_003 provides manual intervention capability when automatic systems are insufficient or disabled, ensuring operational flexibility. llg_004 automates reorder initiation based on threshold breaches, which is the core automatic replenishment logic. llg_005 extends this by automating supplier communication with a confirmation deadline and status logging, which adds supply chain coordination functionality. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time inventory tracking, configurable automatic triggers, manual override, and supplier integration — with no inferred functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

hlg_2860d7ffd5986170_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability for staff to confirm completed orders and manually trigger supplier payments. llg_002 adds the capability for staff to handle partial deliveries and update order status with corresponding inventory adjustments. llg_003 adds the capability for the system to automatically trigger supplier payments upon confirmed complete delivery. llg_004 adds the capability for the system to send automated 48-hour reminders for pending proposal evaluations. llg_005 adds the capability for the system to automatically reject un-evaluated proposals after ten working days and notify suppliers.
